name: implement-plugin-system
description: Implements the BlackAgents plugin system end-to-end — domain lifecycle with install ledger, API routes, runtime-extensible provider registry, /plugins UI, full test coverage, and a gated release review that sends failures back to the developer.
task: Implement the BlackAgents plugin system following the plugin-system skill. Start with Phase 1 (declarative core), then Phase 2 (MCP + provider contributions). Do not touch Tier 3 (code plugins).

steps.instructions: Build the lib/plugins domain per the plugin-system skill. Create: the plugin.json zod manifest schema (manifestVersion 1, unknown keys rejected, minAppVersion gate), discovery of ~/.black-agents/plugins/ via configDir() plus .black-agents/plugins/, validation (bundle path containment, per-artifact type parsing), the install ledger at .black-agents/plugins/installed.json with sha256 hashing, and the install/upgrade/uninstall/disable lifecycle with idempotent semantics and the workspace > plugin > builtin precedence. Add scanPlugins() in lib/artifacts and merge into scanWorkspace; add plugin?: string to Artifact. Plugin artifacts must be excluded from /sync drift and IDE export. Read the plugin-system and nextjs-app-patterns skills, and follow the typescript-strict rule.

Expose the lib/plugins domain over HTTP per the plugin-system skill's API surface: GET/POST /api/plugins, POST /api/plugins/validate (dry run), GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/plugins/:id. All routes use the standard envelope from the api-response-format rule and zod-validate input. Zip uploads must extract only into a temp folder inside the workspace, honouring workspace-filesystem-safety. Error responses must distinguish: invalid manifest, version conflict, namespace collision, missing secret, unapproved MCP server, minAppVersion mismatch. Uninstall returns a removed-vs-kept conflict report.

Implement Phase 2 of the plugin-system skill: merge plugin-declared mcp.json servers (default trust ask, secrets via ${secret:NAME} refs only, never bundled) using lib/mcp/config.ts and lib/mcp/policy.ts, and make the provider registry runtime-extensible — lib/llm/registry.ts currently uses a static Record with a union ProviderId; extend it so plugin providers.json definitions (OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible) can register and unregister without code changes. Install must refuse any bundle shipping executable JS/TS or API keys. Follow the llm-security and llm-output-safety rules.

Build the /plugins page per the plugin-system skill's UI surface: installed list (id, version, artifact counts, edited-artifact conflicts called out prominently), a drop-a-zip install flow with a preview screen showing exactly what will be installed (artifacts, MCP servers with trust prompts, providers, required secrets) before confirmation, and a detail view with README, per-artifact modified badges, disable toggle, upgrade button, and uninstall that surfaces the conflict report with a per-file choice (delete anyway / keep) when artifacts were edited. Use the design-system skill and rule, with full responsive and accessible states (loading, empty, error).

Cover the plugin system per the testing-patterns skill and the testing-required rule. Unit-test the manifest validator (valid, unknown keys, missing files, path escape, executable-code refusal, minAppVersion mismatch) and the lifecycle against a mocked filesystem: install writes the ledger and hashes, upgrade preserves user-edited artifacts as conflicts, uninstall removes unmodified files and keeps modified ones, uninstall is idempotent, two plugins with the same namespaced name are refused. Integration-test the /api/plugins routes including each distinct error case and the envelope shape. Verify plugin artifacts never appear in /sync drift.

Prove the plugin system works end-to-end with Playwright per the testing-patterns skill and the ironbee-devtools-use rule: build a small fixture bundle, then drive the running app — install via the /plugins drop flow, review the preview and approve its MCP server, confirm the plugin's agent/skill appear in the artifacts list, edit one installed artifact, uninstall, and assert the conflict report appears and the unedited artifact is removed while the edited one is kept. Run the full CI-style gate (type-check, lint, tests, build) and report any failures.

The release review rejected the work. Fix every defect in the review feedback. Stay inside the plugin-system skill and the project rules. Do not add new scope. Re-run the checks that failed when you can.

Act as the final pre-production gate. Restate the task's acceptance criteria as a checklist, then verify each one with concrete evidence (file/line citations or prior-step outputs) — criteria without evidence are FAILs. Inspect the work against the typescript-strict, api-response-format, testing-required, design-system, and llm-security rules and the plugin-system, nextjs-app-patterns, and testing-patterns skills. Check the specific seams: workspace-confined filesystem access, no plugin artifacts in /sync drift or IDE export, no secrets or executable code in bundles, response envelopes on every route, no silent artifact shadowing, meaningful (non-vacuous) tests with error paths covered, and loading/empty/error UI states present. End the report with exactly one line: VERDICT: approve or VERDICT: reject followed by numbered, reproducible defects each with a definition of done. You are read-only: never fix, edit, or re-run anything yourself.
